newsitem.title: JAPAN: DuPont, Mitsui petchem plant to restart next week.
newsitem.headline: DuPont, Mitsui petchem plant to restart next week.

text.p: DuPont-Mitsui Polychemical Co Ltd said on Friday its polyethylene plant in Hiroshima Prefecture, western Japan, was set to resume operations next week after closing a week ago due to a minor fire.
DuPont-Mitsui Polychemical is equally owned by DuPont Co and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd.
"We are fairly sure we can secure approval from local authorities to restart the plant by early next week," a company spokesman said.
The plant was shut on April 4 after vapourised ethylene, which was released from safety valves after pressure built up inside a reactor that converts ethylene to polyethylene, caught fire.
No one was injured and no facilities were damaged by the fire, the spokesman said.
Mitsui Petrochemical's Chiba plant near Tokyo supplies feedstock ethylene to the Hiroshima plant, which has the capacity to produce 70,000 tonnes of polyethylene a year.
The Chiba plant has an annual ethylene production capacity of 553,000 tonnes.
